questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, some parts of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

To bring these to you (1)/wherever you are (2)/however you have time (3) / No error (4)/
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is **'however you have time'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

In this given part of the sentence, the usage of **'however'** is incorrect Instead, use** 'whenever'**

 
• According to the rule of grammar, we need to use 'conjunction' that denotes time hence the conjunction 'whenever' shows the time So it is the correct conjunction. Also, it means 'You use whenever to refer to any time or every time that something happens or is true.'
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She always called at the house whenever she was in the area.
 
 

**Correct sentence - **To bring these to you wherever you are** whenever** you have time.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

We will continue to (1)/strive in dark (2)/but we will not driven out (3) / No error (4)/
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of future verb is brought under consideration. Helping verb 'will/shall' takes verb's first form i.e V1. Hence, replace 'driven' with **drive. **Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **We will continue to strive in dark but we will not drive out.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word.Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She cannot deprive him______his rights.
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 3**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. Verb 'deprive' means suffering a severe and damaging lack of basic material and cultural benefits; underprivileged. So, when the subject is deprived of something(noun). Then, preposition 'of' is used. If it is a verb(deprived from going). Then, 'from' is used. Hence, **option 3 i.e. of **is correct answer.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best express the meaning of the given word.**

Awe
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Admiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Awe"** means a feeling of reverential respect mixed with fear or wonder. (विस्मय)

 
 
• **Example: **The tourists were in awe of the magnificent waterfall.
 
 
 
• **"Admiration" **refers to respect and warm approval. (प्रशंसा)
 
 
• **Example: **She looked at her mentor with admiration.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word that best expresses the meaning of "Awe" is "Admiration".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Admiration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Expectation **(अपेक्षा): A strong belief that something will happen or be the case.

 
 
• **Example:** There is a high expectation for the new policy to bring positive change.
 
 
 
• **Familiarity **(परिचय): Close acquaintance with or knowledge of something.
 
 
• **Example: **Her familiarity with the local culture helped her settle in quickly.
 
 
 
• **Calmness** (शांति): The state or quality of being free from agitation or strong emotion.
 
 
• **Example:** He maintained his calmness even under pressure.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Augment
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Degrade.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The opposite in meaning of the word **"augment"** is** "degrade,"** so the correct answer is** option 3.**
 
• The word** "augment" **means **to increase or make something larger in size or quantity**.
 
 
• For example, "She **augmented **her income by taking on a second job" means that she increased her income by taking on a second job.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 3, "degrade," which means to lower in quality, value, or status.
 
 
• For example, "The quality of the product **degraded** over time" means that the quality of the product declined over time.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1, "develop,"** means to grow or progress, and it is not an antonym of **"augment."**

 
 
• For example, "The company is **developing **a new product" means that the company is creating a new product.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "enhance,"** means to improve or make something better. It is not an antonym of "augment," but the two words are related.
 
 
• For example, "The new technology **enhanced **the user experience" means that the new technology improved the user experience.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "increase," **means to make something larger or more numerous. This word is similar in meaning to "augment" but it is not an antonym.
 
 
• For example, "The company **increased **its profits by 20%" means that the company's profits grew by 20%.

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

The opinion

P: opinion of many

Q: great must be the

R: that makes a book
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Firstly, the starter ends with 'opinion'. Hence, it cannot continue with the same word. So, option 3 is eliminated. Also, an article is followed by either a noun or an adjective. Hence, sequence QR in option 4 is incorrect. Since, starter ends with a noun and Q starts with an adjective. But, this is grammatically incorrect because adjective comes before noun. Hence, option 2 is incorrect. Hence, **option 1 i.e. RQP **is the correct answer.

questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

S + 2 = U; U + 2 = W; W + 2 = Y; Y + 2 = **A**

A + 2 = C; C + 2 = E; E + 2 = G; G + 2 = **I**

P – 2 = N; N – 2 = L; L – 2 = J; J – 2 = **H**

Thus, the term that completes the series is AIH.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All pen are chairs.

II. All chairs are tables.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are pen.

II. Some chairs are tables.
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

__
 
• Meaning of **"Some A are B"** in Syllogism - there is **at least one **point in A which is in B.
 
• Meaning of** "All A are B"** in Syllogism - **each point of** A is in B.
 
• This explains why **"some" **can be considered as a subset of **"all".**
 
• Therefore, if **"All A are B" is true, then "some A are B" is always true.**

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/27b5799af20615edb92362bab171e180b7c988b866f5ed669331d1f21d0c7778.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are pen → True (as all pens are chairs given so some chairs are also pens, it is definite hence, true)

II. Some chairs are tables → True (as all chairs are tables given so some chairs are tables also, it is definite, hence, true)

Hence **both the conclusions follow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/307e85e57673f404a8979eb1e7df043b77e9e6be92f7cfb96d6f0f1811a13ce8.png]

questions.question: In a certain code language, **“BOOK” **is written as **“86” **and **“READ” **is written as **“56”. **How will **“GOOD” **be written in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

BOOK → (2 + 15 + 15 + 11) × 2 = 86

READ → (18 + 5 + 1 + 4) × 2 = 56

Similarly,

GOOD → (7 + 15 + 15 + 4) × 2 = **82**

Hence 'GOOD' is coded as 82.

questions.question: Which of the given value is completely divisible by 12?
questions.solution:
When a number is divisible by 3 and 4, then the number is always divisible by 12.

**Rule for 3 **- When the sum of digits is divisible by 3, then the number will always divisible by 3.

**Rule for 4 **- When the last two digits of number is divisible by 4, then the number will always divisible by 4.

⇒ Sum of digits of 3470 = 14, which is not divisible by 3.

⇒ Sum of digits of 7236 = 18 which is divisible by 3 and the last two digits is divisible by 4.

⇒ Sum of digits of 1426 = 13, which is not divisible by 3.

⇒ Sum of digits of 2427 = 15, divisible by 3 but last two digits are not divisible by 4.

Hence, 7236 is divisible by 12.

questions.question: X, Y and Z can complete a work in 15, 45 and 90 days respectively. In how many days X, Y and Z together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
X can complete the work in 15 days

⇒ X’s one day work = 1/15

Y can complete the work in 45 days

⇒ Y’s one day work = 1/45

Z can complete the work in 90 days

⇒ Z’s one day work = 1/90

⇒ X + Y + Z = (1/15 + 1/45 + 1/90)

⇒ X + Y + Z = (6 + 2 + 1)/90 = 1/10

∴ (X + Y + Z) together can complete the work in 10 days

questions.question: U, V and W together can complete a work in 15 days. U alone can complete the work in 60 days. In how many days V and W together can complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given,

(U + V + W) can complete a work in 15 days.

⇒ (U + V + W)’s one day work = 1/15

U alone can complete the work in 60 days.

⇒ U’s one day work = 1/60

⇒ (V + W)’s one day work = (1/15 - 1/60) = (4 - 1)/60 = 1/20

V + W can complete the same work in 20 days.

questions.question: Marked price of an article is 30% more than its cost price. If 30% discount is given, then what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Let the Cost price be Rs. x.

Then, MP = x + 0.3x = 1.3x

After giving discount, we get

⇒ SP = 1.3x - (0.3 × 1.3x) = 0.91x

Loss % = frac{{CP - SP}}{{CP}} times 100

⇒ Loss % = frac{{x - 0.91x}}{x} times 100 = 9\%

questions.question: After giving a discount of 40% on an article, shopkeeper gains 25%. Marked price is how much percent more than the cost price?
questions.solution:
Let the marked price of an article be Rs. X

⇒ SP = x - 0.4x = 0.6x

⇒ Gain % = frac{{SP - CP}}{{CP}} times 100

Rightarrow 25 = frac{{SP - CP}}{{CP}} times 100

⇒ CP = 0.48x

Now,

⇒ MP - CP = x - 0.48x = 0.52x

⇒ % Increase = frac{{0.52x}}{{0.48x}} times 100 = 108.33\%

questions.question: Average of 7 consecutive numbers is A. If 2 numbers which are before these 7 numbers are also taken, then what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
Let the 7 consecutive number be (x - 3), (x - 2), (x - 1), (x), (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3)

The sum of above consecutive number = 7x

⇒ Average of numbers = The sum of above consecutive number/7 = A

⇒ x = A

After adding 2 numbers which are before these 7 numbers, we get

The numbers are (x - 5), (x - 4), (x - 3), (x - 2), (x - 1), (x), (x + 1), (x + 2), (x + 3)

⇒ Sum = 9x - 9

Average = 9(x - 1)/9 = x - 1 = A - 1

questions.question: Which type of plants have their branches in the upper part of the stem, much above the ground?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Trees.**

__**E
xplanation-**__

**Shrubs:** Shrubs are medium-sized, woody plants taller than herbs and have multiple stems. However, they are smaller than trees. Their branches grow near the base, close to the ground and are usually dense and bushy. Examples include azaleas and boxwood.

**Trees: **Trees are the largest plants, and they have a single woody stem or trunk that extends a significant distance above the ground before dividing into branches. The branches of trees primarily grow from the upper part of the stem, well above the ground. Mature trees are typically capable of withstanding all seasons. Examples include oak trees, maple trees, and pine trees.

**Herbs:** Herbs are small, non-woody and flowering plants. They complete their life cycle in one or two seasons. The term "herb" is also used to describe plants that have medicinal properties or are used for their flavor or scent. Examples include grasses, wheat, and tulips.

questions.question: The distance travelled by a freely falling body is proportional to which among the following?

options.text: The square of the time of fall
The square root of the time of fall

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• Velocity of the particle is defined as the rate of change of its displacement and can be expressed as

vec v = frac{{overrightarrow {dx} }}{{dt}}

 
• And acceleration of the particle is defined as the rate of change of its velocity and can be expressed as

vec a = frac{{overrightarrow {dv} }}{{dt}}

 
• Whereas motion of particles can be predicted using Kinematic equations and they are given as
 
• S = ut + (1)/(2)a{t²}
 
• v = u + at
 
• {v²} = {u²} + 2as

Here,

Displacement of particle = S

Initial velocity = u

Final velocity = v

Acceleration of particle = a

Time period at any instant = t

**Explanation:**__

From the above given explanation, we can see that if a body is falling freely under gravity the body will be accelerated towards the ground at the rate of g and it can be expressed as shown below

h = (0)t + (1)/(2)g{t²}

here, displacement is considered as h and initial velocity will be zero since the body was at rest initially

Hence distance travelled by freely falling body is h = (1)/(2)g{t²}

So, the **distance travelled **by a freely falling body is **proportional to the square of the time of fall.**

questions.question: Molecules in Solids______
